Real exam mechanics CONFIRMED directly from the handbook's own text (primary official source, not an aggregator): the Class D (non-commercial) knowledge test consists of 40 questions, and an applicant can miss up to six (6) questions before failing -- i.e. at least 34/40 (85 percent) correct is required to pass. Quoted directly: 'The knowledge test consists of 40 questions; you can miss up to six (6) questions before failing the test.' A failed knowledge test requires a 3-day wait and repayment of the $5.00 test fee before retesting. The companion skills (driving) test requires 12 or fewer errors to pass. Timed-vs-untimed status for the knowledge test is NOT stated anywhere in the handbook and could not be confirmed from ITD's site pages either -- left explicitly unconfirmed rather than guessed. Content-depth rationale: this is an unusually substantive 139-page manual (far longer than many state driver handbooks) covering licensing documents/GDL/permit types in detail, required equipment specifications with exact distances and measurements (brakes, headlights, mirrors, horns, tires, turn signals), a full signs/signals/pavement-markings chapter including modern intersection types (roundabouts, thru-turns, SPUI, DDI), detailed traffic law sections (speed, stopping, turns, right-of-way, passing, parking, following distance, freeway driving), a distracted/defensive driving chapter, an extensive sharing-the-road chapter (pedestrians, horseback riders, bicyclists, motorcycles, large vehicles, open range, wildlife), a weather/night/emergency-driving chapter (hydroplaning, flash floods, winter driving, skidding, ABS), and a detailed penalties chapter (point system table, GDL penalty tiers, administrative license suspension, DUI BAC thresholds and criminal penalties by offense count, open container law). This comfortably supports a rich, non-repetitive bank; 262 questions were written across 16 topic buckets, each grounded in and cited to specific quoted manual text (see source_note per question), with no invented facts, no reuse of the handbook's own printed practice-test questions, and no filler 'common driving knowledge' outside what the manual actually states. This is a brand-new Idaho Driver track -- no prior ID driver content exists on the site.
